includedPullRequests.title: fixes crash when uploading carb entry without id to Tidepool issue #1425
includedPullRequests.body:
closes #1425

CarbsEntry+LoopKit.swift force unwrapped the id when building the SyncCarbObject:
`uuid: UUID(uuidString: id!)` -> `uuid: id.flatMap(UUID.init(uuidString:))`

no random UUID as fallback, so the carb keeps the same identity between uploads.

this is a follow up on #709 by @Sjoerd-Bo3 (closed as stale). it uses the change @kingst  suggested in the review there, and checks what Tidepool does with a carb without uuid.

carb without id: TidepoolService builds no datum for it, so nothing is sent. it stays not uploaded and is checked again only inside the 24 h upload window. other carbs upload normally.

tests in TrioTests/CarbsEntryLoopKitTests.swift:
- nil id: no crash, uuid and syncIdentifier are nil (crashes with the old `id!` code)
- UUID id: uuid and syncIdentifier match the id

tested on Tidepool with a simulator build:
- signed in to Tidepool, added 10 g carb, uploaded
- removed its id in the local store, added 20 g carb
- no crash, 20 g uploaded, the carb without id skipped
- Tidepool export shows 10 g and 20 g once each, no duplicates
- the simulator sign-in to Tidepool crashed in TidepoolKit DNS.swift:180 (unaligned load); a local loadUnaligned patch was used for this test only, not part of this PR

includedPullRequests.title: feat(nightscout): Hide the backfill button once Nightscout has been checked
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Readings the Dexcom sensor never delivered aren't in Nightscout either, so the Home backfill button kept coming back after "No new readings found". Trio now remembers the last successful Nightscout check and stops offering gaps it already covered.

```diff
 hasMissingReadings(readings, now)
+  if the sensor is warming up → hide
+  lastCheck = last successful check for this Nightscout URL (ignored once > 24 h old)
+  drop readings before lastCheck; lastCheck counts as a reading
   any two readings > 7.5 min apart → show
-  newest reading > 7.5 min old → show
+  newest reading or lastCheck > 10 min old → show   # time for late uploads to reach Nightscout
```

```text
NightscoutBackfill.run()            # Home button and Settings button
  fetchAndStore(last 24 h)
    fetch → save new readings
    if both succeeded and the page held < 1600 entries
      NightscoutBackfillChecks.record(now, url)   # one UserDefaults key
  publish checkedThrough            # Home button hides right away, not on the next 30 s tick
```

The Settings button behaves as before: it always fetches the full 24 hours, so it still works when a reading reaches Nightscout after a check.

## Evidence

- **Before:** with stubs in place of the new behaviour, 8 of the new tests in `NightscoutBackfillTests` fail, for example:
  ```text
  gap the last check covered          → button still shown
  CGM 10 min behind, checked 10 min ago → button shown (was 7.5 min)
  sensor warming up                   → button shown
  successful backfill                 → no check recorded
  ```
  **After:** both `Nightscout backfill` suites and `NightscoutBackfillLayoutTests` pass. Full suite: 1,157 tests. The only failure is `FileStorageTests` "Can parse mmol/L settings to mg/dL", which is known to be flaky and passes when run alone.

Not tried on a device or in the simulator yet.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Adds one UserDefaults key (`trio.nightscoutBackfill.lastCheck.v1`) and no Core Data changes. Reverting leaves that key unused and harmless.

**Blast Radius:** small

It only changes when the Home backfill button shows. Fetching, duplicate filtering and saving work as before. Trade-off: a reading that reaches Nightscout after a check won't be offered from Home. The Settings button still fetches it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
